genZNote: Group B strep. Bacitracin-resistant, unlike Group A sitting one letter away on the alphabet and one test away on the plate.

habitat.hostAssociation: Colonizes vagina/rectum in 10-30% of pregnant individuals

culture.media: Blood agar, Lim broth (selective enrichment for prenatal screening)
culture.colonyMorphology: Grayish-white colonies with a narrow zone of beta-hemolysis
culture.hemolysis: Beta-hemolytic (narrow zone, less prominent than group A strep)

identificationClues: Bacitracin resistant — distinguishes from group A strep

diseases: Neonatal sepsis and meningitis (early- and late-onset)
Invasive infection in older adults with comorbidities
clinicalImportance.transmission: Vertical transmission from colonized mother to neonate during birth
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Leading cause of neonatal sepsis and meningitis worldwide; routine prenatal screening (35-37 weeks) with intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis has greatly reduced early-onset disease
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: CAMP test positivity and bacitracin resistance are the classic bedside differentiators from Streptococcus pyogenes

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: CAMP positive, bacitracin resistant, hippurate positive
examFacts.importantTest: CAMP test (arrowhead hemolysis with S. aureus streak)
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Bacitracin resistance distinguishes it from bacitracin-sensitive Group A Streptococcus
